evidence.field: bronze and small-seal forms; graph explanation
evidence.text: The database records a bronze form indexed as 集成00068 and a small-seal form in 說文. It describes 止 above 舟 as indicating a boat moving forward. This is a recorded graph interpretation; the page does not date the first lexical sense.
evidence.title: 漢字「前」：字形演變

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00355-003 research note; quoted Shuowen and later graph-history accounts
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen account for 歬, “moving forward” and formed from 止 over 舟. It also preserves competing accounts: Duan Yucai says 前, associated with even cutting, was later used for directional 歬; other lexicographers say 歬 was the original graph and 前 developed from a cutting graph. The entry calls 歬 a variant of 前, but does not resolve the historical order.
evidence.title: [A00355-003] 歬 (前) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: Chinese glyph origin and Zhengzhang phonetic series
evidence.text: The entry reports the analysis 剪 as a phono-semantic graph with 歬 as phonetic and 刀 as semantic, and gives Zhengzhang (2003) readings for 前 and 歬 as *zleːn and 剪 as *ʔslenʔ. These are explicitly Zhengzhang system reconstructions, not Baxter–Sagart readings. Its narrative derivation is secondary and does not establish a separately named tool as the source of a whole-graph loan.

gaps: No independently opened official Unihan records for 歬, 舟, or 止 were obtained; local supplied rows are reported separately and are not treated as external evidence.

No Baxter–Sagart row for 歬 or 剪 was verified externally or supplied locally here. Do not compare their readings to 前 in the Baxter–Sagart system. The opened 剪 page's *zleːn comparison is specifically Zhengzhang (2003).
The Commons file lead was not directly opened and its original pixels were not inspected. Do not select it as a verified historical glyph asset based on search output alone.

The competing accounts about directional 歬 and a cutting graph remain unresolved. No independent historical name and pronunciation for a depicted implement were established, so an object-name sound loan cannot be asserted.
The Sinica database identifies an indexed bronze form, but this research did not verify a dated primary inscription passage establishing the earliest lexical sense or semantic chronology.
